The 1926 Slavery Convention’s Centennial in Context
news.summary_en: What do you do when you realize moral failure has underwritten your life? This is the story beyond the 1926 Slavery Convention, which was deeply imperfect, but 100 years ago constituted the international community's first attempt at ending the moral scourge of slavery.

news.title: Xi Jinping’s Return to Washington: A State Visit to Build Stability
news.summary_en: Xi’s visit to Washington is likely to be heavy on optics and symbolism but light on substantive progress, highlighting both leaders’ conviction that each is the only one who can manage the other and that regular meetings are necessary to stabilize the bilateral relationship.

news.title: He Said, Xi Said
news.summary_en: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch discusses potential outcomes of the upcoming summit between President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Washington.

news.title: What Iran and Ukraine Reveal About OSINT in War
news.summary_en: The war with Iran and Russia's war on Ukraine hold a critical lesson for the United States: just how little control it may have over how foreign adversaries collect and exploit open-source intelligence against its interests.

news.title: Understanding the U.S. Federal Government’s AI Spending
news.summary_en: Federal agencies obligated $4.1 billion across 2,255 AI-related contracts since FY 2019, and 83 percent of those dollars went to the Defense Department. The CSIS Futures Lab follows the money trail and tracks the evolution of federal AI demand.

news.title: The State of AI Global Governance and Its Implications for the U.S.-China Summit
news.summary_en: In a new report, Chris Collins and Aalok Mehta analyze the global AI governance landscape and outline how Washington should approach AI talks at the upcoming U.S.-China summit.

news.title: The Levantine Opportunity in a Churning Middle East
news.summary_en: The wars of the past three years have eroded the fragile order of the Middle East. Now, for the first time in decades, the Levant has a chance to create a new alignment and build a regional order centered around strong, inclusive states, stability, and open trade.

news.title: What Would an Interim U.S.-Mexico Trade Deal Actually Involve?
news.summary_en: Mexico is close to an interim deal with the United States. What it concedes for tariff relief today could set the baseline for North America down the line.

news.title: Rethinking Export Controls as a Tool in Modern Technology Competition
news.summary_en: Export controls can delay China’s technological progress, but they cannot secure lasting U.S. leadership. This report examines the limits and costs of semiconductor controls and argues for pairing targeted restrictions with sustained investment in U.S. innovation.

news.title: Behind the Headlines: What Motivates and Moves Japanese Elite Opinion on Nuclear Weapons Acquisition
news.summary_en: A CSIS Japan Chair survey shows that the majority of Japanese strategic elites oppose nuclear weapons acquisition despite a worsening security environment—but these attitudes could shift if South Korea acquires the bomb or the United States reduces its military presence.
